title: Tensegrity table
summary: the top hangs, the cables hold it
description: The floating table: a top hanging from a hook on the base by one short rope and held level by three to six tensioned outer cables. Set the size, the cables and the load; the Jig sizes every tension and refuses a load the fittings cannot carry.
process: CNC routing of plywood (hooks and plates), drilling, wire rope assembly with ferrules and turnbuckles

difficulty.rationale: Coupled statics in formulas, slanted revolves, count-driven topology, multi-body booleans.

standards: EN 1995-1-1 (Eurocode 5): kmod 0.60 (permanent, service class 1), kdef 0.80, gamma_M 1.2 for plywood, table 3.1 to 3.2 and 9.1 as summarised in Design of timber structures, vol. 2
Metsä Wood Declaration of Performance, birch plywood: characteristic bending, compression, tension and shear strengths, 13-ply
DIN 582 stainless eye nuts: working load limits (S3i)
AISI 316 7x7 wire rope: minimum breaking loads and masses (GS Products); E = 57.3 kN/mm2 (S3i)
316 stainless eye-and-eye turnbuckles: lengths and safe working loads (Blue Bottle Marine)
materials: Birch plywood, 18 to 24 mm (walnut, oak or birch face veneer)
AISI 316 7x7 wire rope, 2 to 4 mm, with copper ferrules and thimbles
316 stainless eye/eye turnbuckles M5 or M6, DIN 582 eye nuts M6 or M8, M6 socket screws, DIN 9021 washers, steel M8 barrel nuts (12 x 18 mm) and M8 rod
Epoxy or PU glue; soft self-adhesive sponge-rubber strip for the rim
